notes: Perfect claim overlap (C6, C66, C67, C68, C69, C89). LLM finds evidence sufficient for SEC24A-specific PCSK9 dependence using co-IP, overexpression, and siRNA data. Reviewers accept the data but require additional direct mechanistic experiments (SEC24A knockdown in budding assays or knockout liver cytosol) before concluding support.

High claim overlap (C4, C49, C50, C76). Both agree that epistasis experiments with Apoe and Ldlr mutations demonstrate receptor-mediated clearance mechanism. Peer review also includes C5 (LDLR upregulation) which strengthens their acceptance.

Strong claim overlap (C2, C30, C31, C32, C33). Both agree SEC24A deficiency is compatible with normal survival and development. LLM includes additional allele claims (C29, C34, C40) not explicitly mentioned by reviewers, but core conclusion is identical.

Good claim overlap (C8, C102, C103). Both agree that PCSK9 represents selective COPII-dependent secretion of soluble cargo, challenging bulk flow models. Reviewers additionally suggest this implies a cargo receptor may exist.

Strong claim overlap (C3, C38, C39, C40). Both agree on marked reduction in plasma cholesterol across multiple measurements and alleles. LLM includes additional protein data (C35, C36) and C28 not explicitly in peer review, but core cholesterol phenotype is agreed upon.

Moderate claim overlap (C59, C61, C62, C63, C64). LLM finds convergent evidence from multiple approaches sufficient to support COPII-mediated ER exit of PCSK9. Reviewers acknowledge the evidence but require additional direct mechanistic experiments with SEC24A-depleted or knockout cytosol.

Exact claim overlap (C116, C121) on therapeutic potential. LLM rates as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of human validation. Reviewers are stronger, rating UNSUPPORTED and explicitly stating therapeutic claims should be de-emphasized due to additional phenotypic effects (RBC changes, SCD1 reduction).

Partial claim overlap (C7, C91, C92). Both agree on partial overlap in cargo selectivity between SEC24A and SEC24B, distinct from SEC24C/D. LLM includes additional in vitro budding data (C70, C71, C73) not explicitly mentioned by reviewers.

Minimal claim overlap (C54 only). Both agree on reduced plasma PCSK9 and its role in the mechanism. LLM groups this with LDLR upregulation and IDOL data (C5, C51-C55), while peer review groups PCSK9 reduction with ER retention data (C57, C58).

Minimal claim overlap (C57, C58) on PCSK9 ER retention. LLM finds Endo H sensitivity data sufficient as part of broader COPII evidence. Reviewers question blot quality and request use of different antibody, rating as UNCERTAIN.

Minimal claim overlap (C53 only) on IDOL levels. LLM finds unchanged IDOL sufficient to rule out alternative LDLR regulation. Reviewers request explicit discussion of IDOL and other mechanisms, rating as UNCERTAIN until addressed.

Minimal claim overlap (C34 only) on blood count changes. Both accept mild RBC changes (MCV, MCHC increases) as real findings. Reviewers use this to argue against therapeutic potential, while LLM includes it as part of normal development assessment.

Minimal claim overlap (C5 only) on LDLR upregulation. Both agree LDLR is increased. LLM groups this with PCSK9 reduction mechanism (C51-C55), while peer review groups with epistasis experiments (C4, C49, C50, C76). Different groupings but same conclusion.

Claims C41-C44 on liver-specific deletion appear only in LLM results. LLM rates as UNCERTAIN due to incomplete deletion and smaller effect size compared to full knockout. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

Claims C46, C90 on selective PCSK9 effect without disrupting SREBP signaling appear only in LLM results. LLM finds this supports cargo-specific function. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

Claims C93, C94 on SEC24A/B balanced pools and post-transcriptional compensation appear only in LLM results. LLM finds evidence of distinct functional pools. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
